example: Example run with fictional figures: Northbrook Trading, September under review, scan window 1 July to 31 October. The figures match the worked examples on the step-by-step page.

chosen.Duplicate_Invoice_Scan_2026-11-02.xlsx: the file name that the skill gives the workpaper, dated on the day of the run, after the scan window closes

messages.text: Can you check our supplier bills for duplicates? September is the month I care about.
Yes. Before I read anything, I need some answers. I ask them all at once, so the run does not stop again for each one.
list: Do you want me to use MosoFin, or will you upload files?
Which company? If you have a group, do I also scan across the companies?
Which period do I scan, and how far back before it? Duplicates often cross a month end.
Which suppliers bill the same amount on purpose, such as rent, insurance or software?
I use Standard sensitivity and a 7-day window for near dates. Do you want Strict or Permissive instead?
Do you have results from an earlier scan?

messages.text: Use MosoFin. Northbrook Trading only. Scan 1 July to 31 October around September. Our landlord, our insurer and three software suppliers bill the same every month. Standard is fine. No earlier scan.

messages.label: Checked the workspace and the company file
rows: Bill search readable, no bank details
messages.summary: The agent can read your books. It cannot change them.

messages.text: Here is my plan. I scan **every bill and payment** at **Northbrook Trading** from **1 July to 31 October**, read through MosoFin. I use **Standard** sensitivity and a **7-day** window. Your landlord, insurer and three software suppliers count as normal repeat billers.
messages.after: **Rule 7 cannot run here.** It finds two suppliers that share one bank account, and MosoFin cannot see bank details. Who can check that in your banking system? Shall I start?

messages.text: The bank's payments team can check it. Yes, go ahead.

messages.label: Read the whole population in one batch
messages.summary: 11 reads, each one to its last page. Nothing in your books changed.

messages.text: I scanned all **1,284 bills** from 212 suppliers, and 1,197 payments. Five clusters look like duplicates. The exposure leaves out the one bill in each cluster that is real.

messages.after: Summit also bills $950 on the 1st of each month. That is a pattern, so only the 6 Sep bill is a suspect.

messages.text: Under **Standard**, the headline counts High and Very High only:
messages.after: D and E are Medium, $1,930 together. They stay on the list, below the headline. Under Strict, the headline is $11,240.

messages.text: Most duplicates are honest errors, not fraud. Here is what I propose, unpaid first:

card.title: Recovery plan
head: Action
Amount
Cluster
rows: Void the open Pinnacle bill before you pay it
Ask Crestline for a credit, a refund or a set-off
Ask Harbor for a credit on its next invoice
Merge the two Pinnacle records and the two Acme records

messages.after: That is $3,200.00 caught before payment and $6,110.00 paid out to recover. For the two paid duplicates, I draft an entry for a person to post. A merge is not reversible in most systems, so check each pair first. I void nothing, merge nothing and ask no supplier for money.

messages.text: Harbor also owes **you** money. Credit note CN-0011 for **$410.00** is still open, and you paid three later Harbor bills in full. It is not a duplicate, so it is not in the exposure.
I ran 9 of the 10 rules. Rule 7 did not run, and the bank's payments team owns it. So this scan found the duplicate errors. It does not show that the fraud test passed.
messages.after: Your workpaper has seven sheets, with a column for your decision on each cluster. Do you want it as an Excel file?
Do you want me to save your settings for next month?

messages.text: Done. I saved your repeat billers, the Standard setting, the 7-day window, the recovery steps and who runs Rule 7. I never save bank details, invoice data or any suspicion about a person.
